itemListElement.name: Best NFT News Outlets to Pitch in 2026

mainEntity.name: Which outlets actually cover NFT news in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: The core list is CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Decrypt, The Block, Blockworks, nft now, Forbes' crypto vertical, TechCrunch for funding-scale stories, and niche newsletters like Bankless for analysis pieces. Each one wants a different version of the same story, so the right move is matching your angle to the desk, not blasting all of them identically.

mainEntity.name: What kind of NFT story still gets covered by trade press?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three angles reliably clear the bar: measurable utility tied to a real number, a named brand or IP partnership, and regulatory or legal firsts. A plain mint or collection launch with no mechanic and no number attached rarely gets picked up anymore, since editors redirected most drop-focused coverage toward tokenization and gaming after 2022.

mainEntity.name: Should I pitch all NFT outlets at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The stronger sequence is one exclusive placement 24 to 48 hours ahead of the announcement, a day-of wave to the remaining relevant outlets with individual, specific pitches, then a follow-up angle a week or two later to extend the story. Pitching everyone the same email on day one usually gets you several polite declines instead of coverage. The full mechanics are in the crypto media relations guide.

mainEntity.name: How much does an NFT PR push cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A launch sprint around a single announcement typically runs $15,000 to $40,000. Ongoing fractional support runs $5,000 to $12,000 a month versus $15,000 to $45,000 for a full agency retainer. Adding creator amplification runs from $200 to $1,500 per post for nano influencers up to $10,000 to $30,000 for mid-tier creators, depending on reach needed.

mainEntity.name: Do reporters still cover NFTs the same way they did in 2021?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most dedicated NFT desks folded into broader crypto, gaming or culture beats after volume collapsed in 2022, and the reporters left on this beat are more selective. Coverage now favors utility, real numbers and named partnerships over drop announcements, which is a higher bar but a fairer one for projects with a genuine story.
